issues.current: Medicaid aide wage $14.57/hr. Notes say the $13.75 (2027) and $15.00 (2028) minimum wage steps come "from a secondary summary only (enacted text not verified)".
issues.correct: The steps are enacted. SB1/HB1 were signed on April 9, 2026. The minimum wage is $13.75 on 1/1/2027 and $15.00 on 1/1/2028, then indexed annually. A $14.57 aide wage is lawful in 2026 and 2027, but it is below the legal minimum from 1/1/2028.
issues.evidence: Governor's release: the legislation "will then increase the minimum wage to $13.75 per hour on January 1, 2027" and then to $15.00 on January 1, 2028.
issues.fix: Change the notes to say the schedule is enacted, citing the Governor's release or DOLI. Model Medicaid aide wage as max($14.57, statutory minimum): $13.75 in 2027 and at least $15.00 from 1/1/2028. Remodel the mixed60 and medicaid100 margins at $15.00, which is about 3% above $14.57 before the 17.5% burden. Treat any Medicaid aide pay below $15.00 from 1/1/2028 as a legal violation. Also update checklist items 9 and 32 to show the 2027 and 2028 steps.

issues.correct: S26 publishes only an annual Virginia home health aide median of $75,504 (2024 survey). $33.00 is a derived figure: $75,504 ÷ (44 hrs × 52 wks) = $33.00. The newer 2025 national median is $35/hr. The Virginia hourly rate was not published.
issues.evidence: Genworth (3/4/2025): Virginia Home Health Aide 2024 annual cost $75,504; national $77,792.
issues.fix: Label the $33 rate as "derived: $75,504 ÷ 2,288 hrs (44 hrs/wk × 52); 2024 survey; operator assumption". Test sensitivity at the 2025 national $35 and at local competitor rates.

issues.json_path: opex[item=Home care scheduling, billing and EVV-interface software].notes; fees_and_timelines_in_checklist[i=42]
issues.current: EVV is required for agency-directed Medicaid aides from 10/1/2026 [S21].
issues.correct: The 10/1/2026 change eliminates the live-in caregiver exemption. After that date, all agency-directed aides and consumer-directed attendants for personal care, respite and companion services must use EVV. EVV for non-live-in aides was already required.
issues.evidence: Bulletin: "Effective October 1, 2026, all agency-directed aides and consumer-directed attendants ... will be required to use an EVV-compliant method".
issues.fix: Reword to: "EVV is already required for non-live-in Medicaid aides; from 10/1/2026 the live-in exemption ends and all agency-directed aides must use EVV." Budget EVV software from day one for any Medicaid configuration.

issues.current: 12 hours of annual training is presented as a DMAS Medicaid requirement. Adopting 12 hours for all aides is described as a "defensible standard".
issues.correct: The VDH HCO personal-care regulation text (12VAC5-381, as published in the 2011 Register) also requires in-service training for home attendants of at least 12 hours annually. This applies to private-pay aides too. I could not retrieve the current section text, so confirm it.
issues.evidence: Register text: "in-service education or training for home attendants shall consist of at least 12 hours annually".
issues.fix: Say 12 hours/year in-service training is a likely VDH licensure requirement for all home attendants (confirm in the current Part IV/V text on LIS). Do not call it optional for private-pay aides. Also note that 12VAC5-381-360 requires RN supervision on a schedule set by the RN and policy, "not to exceed 90 days" (2017 text). The RN hours should cover at least this cadence and the RN-written service plan for every client. Current text unverified.

issues.json_path: payroll_burden.benefits_pct; fees_and_timelines_in_checklist (no paid-sick-leave or overtime item)
issues.current: Benefits 3% "cover paid time and training". No mention of Virginia paid sick leave or FLSA overtime/travel-time rules.
issues.correct: Va. Code §§40.1-33.3–.6 already requires 1 hr of paid sick leave per 30 hrs worked (cap 40 hrs/yr) for covered home health workers. By its definition this applies to consumer-directed Medicaid workers. SB199/HB5 (signed 5/20/2026) extends paid sick leave to most employees. Secondary sources say it phases in from 7/1/2027 for employers with 50 or more employees.
issues.evidence: Groom Law: "On May 20, 2026, Governor Spanberger signed SB 199/HB 5, a new statewide Paid Sick Leave" program.
issues.fix: Add a checklist item and cost line for paid sick leave: about 3.3% of hours worked is the statutory accrual rate (1/30), if it applies to the agency's workforce. Confirm applicability and timing with DOLI or counsel. Add a checklist note that federal FLSA overtime and compensable inter-client travel time apply to agency-employed aides (unverifiable here; confirm with the U.S. DOL). Do not rely on the 3% benefits line to cover both paid sick leave and training.
